newsitem.title: UK: Manchester Utd hits high on prematch nerves.
newsitem.headline: Manchester Utd hits high on prematch nerves.

text.p: Shares in Manchester United Plc hit a record high in modest trading on Wednesday morning ahead of the premier league soccer club's European Champion's league match against Rapid Vienna tonight, analysts said.
The stock hit a new high of 590p at about 1130 GMT, 17p up from yesterday's record close, and has since dropped to orbit around 578p.
"This is typical volatility we see in this stock ahead of crucial games," said Wise Speke research director Vinay Bedi. "A win could have a big upside on revenues," he added.
"People will be holding off until tonight's result," said one marketmaker. He added that shares could move 20p either way depending on how the British champions fare.

Bedi estimated that the club would stand to gain 1.5 million stg if they got through to the quarter finals of the highly lucrative competition. He said they would make the same again on subsequent wins in the tournament.

Manchester must win to be assured of a place in the next round. A draw would put their fate in the hands of the other game in the group between Italy's Juventus and Turkish champions Fenerbahce. If the Turks better Manchester's performance tonight, they qualify. Juventus are already through.
"It's the biggest game Manchester United are playing for a long time" said the marketmaker.
The stock was pushed to a previous record close yesterday after UBS praised the shares' quality and said it had "arguably the strongest brand in the game."

Separately a report in the Independent newspaper said Pearson Television chief executive Greg Dyke and another television executive had predicted the eclipse of broadcasters such as BSkyB by soccer clubs.

The newspaper said Dyke told a seminar on the business of sport that the soaring value of sports rights would bring "untold riches" to clubs such as Manchester United at the expense of programme distributors.
